newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace slips on Thomson news.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace slips on Thomson news.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc (BA) slipped 1.5 percent on Wednesday, shortly after the French government put on hold its privatisation of Thomson SA for which BA's partner Lagardere Groupe was a key bidder.
British Aerospace shares were down 17-1/2 pence at 1132-1/2p at 1025GMT, despite BA's earlier announcement that it had signed a consortium deal to buy German naval unit STN Atlas Electronik.
"Basically, it's off because of the Thomson announcement," said an analyst at Societe Generale. "It's bad news for BA, who were pretty confident they would benefit from the sale."

The French Finance Ministry said it suspended the sale of state-owned electronics and defence giant Thomson because favoured bidder Lagardere Groupe's plan to sell off a multimedia division had been disapproved.

BA's statement earlier on Wednesday that it had signed a deal with German partners Rheinmetall AG and Badenwerk AG to buy former Bremer Vulkan unit STN Atlas Electronik had no noticable uplift on BA shares.

"It was a pretty small positive," said the Societe Generale analyst, although Chris Avery of Paribas acknowledged the buy, which would give BA a 49 percent interest in the business for about 270 million marks, as a "useful step forwards".
Shares in Thomson and Lagardere were suspended shortly before the French government announcement.
But General Electric saw its shares up two pence as analysts said they saw it back in the running for Thomson.
One analyst suggested GEC could now be a preferred buyer for Thomson if it offered to retain the multimedia division.
